Two classic traps: one catches Black after 1.d4, one catches White after 1.e4. Both are over in a few moves. ♟️

Which side do you usually play? 👇

ig_caption:
Two classic opening traps, one for each side of the board.

After 1.d4: in the Queen's Gambit Accepted, Black takes the c4 pawn and tries to keep it with ...b5. After 4.a4 c6 5.axb5 cxb5?? White plays 6.Qf3, and the queen hits the rook on a8 along the long diagonal. Black can't save everything and loses at least a piece. The usual fix: let the pawn go and develop your pieces.

After 1.e4: in the Stafford Gambit, Black gives a pawn for quick play. After 5.d3 Bc5 6.Bg5?? Black plays 6...Nxe4! If 7.Bxd8, then 7...Bxf2+ 8.Ke2 Bg4 is checkmate. If 7.dxe4 instead, 7...Bxf2+ 8.Kxf2 Qxd1 wins White's queen.

The habit that stops both: before a natural-looking move, look for your opponent's checks and long lines.

Which side do you usually play? 👇

slides.title: 1.d4 or 1.e4?
slides.title2: A trap waits on each side.
slides.sub: TWO CLASSIC TRAPS, OVER IN A FEW MOVES
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Bg5 Nxe4 Bxd8 Bxf2+ Ke2 Bg4#

slides.title: After 1.d4: the greedy pawn
slides.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5
slides.take: In the Queen's Gambit Accepted, Black takes the c4 pawn. Then 3...b5 tries to keep it.
slides.edge: It looks natural to hold on to an extra pawn. But the b-pawn and c-pawn leave the long diagonal to the a8 rook.

slides.title: 6.Qf3: the long diagonal
slides.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Qf3
slides.take: White's queen hits the a8 rook along the long diagonal. Black can't save everything and loses at least a piece.
slides.edge: The usual fix: let the c4 pawn go. White wins it back, and Black gets on with moving pieces out.

slides.title: After 1.e4: the pin
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Bg5 Nxe4
slides.take: Black has given a pawn. 6.Bg5?? pins the f6 knight to the queen. Or so it seems: 6...Nxe4! moves it anyway.
slides.edge: If 7.dxe4, then 7...Bxf2+ 8.Kxf2 Qxd1 wins White's queen.

slides.title: Take the queen, lose the game
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Bg5 Nxe4 Bxd8 Bxf2+ Ke2 Bg4#
slides.take: 7.Bxd8 grabs the queen. 7...Bxf2+ drives the king to e2, and 8...Bg4 is checkmate.
slides.edge: Every square around the king is covered or blocked. A queen up, and the game is over.

slides.title: Look for checks and long lines
slides.body: Both traps start with a move that looks natural: keep the pawn, pin the knight. Before you play it, look at every check and every long diagonal your opponent could use.
slides.note: The move that looks the most obvious deserves the quickest check.
